metadata.description: Extracted statistics from peer-reviewed research on ADHD comorbidities: prison populations, substance use disorder, and suicide risk
metadata.note: All data manually extracted from abstracts and full-text articles. No downloadable datasets available for these studies.

adhd_in_prison_populations.citation: Fazel S, Favril L. Prevalence of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder in adult prisoners: An updated meta-analysis. Crim Behav Ment Health. 2024;34(3):339-346.

pooled_adhd_prevalence_random_sampling.interpretation: 1 in 12 adults in prison diagnosed with ADHD

adhd_in_prison_populations.notes: Updated meta-analysis correcting for overestimation in prior reviews by using only unselected samples

adhd_in_prison_populations.citation: Young S, Moss D, Sedgwick O, Fridman M, Hodgkins P. A meta-analysis of the prevalence of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder in incarcerated populations. Psychol Med. 2015;45(2):247-258.
adhd_in_prison_populations.population: incarcerated populations (youth and adult, male and female)
adhd_in_prison_populations.notes: Largest meta-analysis on this topic. Screening tools produce significantly higher (false-positive) rates than diagnostic interviews.

adhd_in_prison_populations.citation: Ginsberg Y, Hirvikoski T, Lindefors N. Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) among longer-term prison inmates is a prevalent, persistent and disabling disorder. BMC Psychiatry. 2010;10:112.
adhd_in_prison_populations.population: longer-term male inmates, high-security Swedish prison

adhd_prevalence.interpretation: Estimated prevalence among longer-term male inmates

childhood_diagnosis_rate.note: Only 2 of 30 had childhood ADHD diagnosis despite most needing services

adhd_in_prison_populations.notes: Small sample but rich comorbidity data. All confirmed ADHD cases had lifetime SUD. Striking underdiagnosis in childhood.

adhd_and_substance_use_disorder.citation: van Emmerik-van Oortmerssen K, van de Glind G, van den Brink W, Smit F, Crunelle CL, Swets M, Schoevers RA. Prevalence of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder in substance use disorder patients: a meta-analysis and meta-regression analysis. Drug Alcohol Depend. 2012;122(1-2):11-19.

overall_adhd_prevalence_in_sud.interpretation: Almost 1 in 4 SUD patients meet DSM criteria for comorbid ADHD

by_substance.cocaine_dependence: lower ADHD prevalence than other substances

adhd_and_substance_use_disorder.notes: Widely cited foundational meta-analysis. Prevalence depends on substance type and assessment instrument.

adhd_and_substance_use_disorder.citation: Rohner H, Gaspar N, Philipsen A, Schulze M. Prevalence of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) among Substance Use Disorder (SUD) Populations: Meta-Analysis. Int J Environ Res Public Health. 2023;20(2):1275.

overall_adhd_prevalence_in_sud.interpretation: Approximately 1 in 5 SUD patients have comorbid ADHD

adhd_and_substance_use_disorder.notes: Updated meta-analysis including more recent studies. Consistent with 2012 findings. High heterogeneity across studies.

adhd_and_substance_use_disorder.citation: Moldekleiv CJ, Lundervold AJ, Solberg BS, Engeland A, Fadnes LT, Chalabianloo F, Klungsøyr K. Prevalence of substance use disorder in individuals with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder: associations with sex and psychiatric comorbidity. BMC Psychiatry. 2025;25:936.
adhd_and_substance_use_disorder.notes: Large-scale sex-stratified study. ADHD with comorbid psychiatric disorders dramatically increases SUD prevalence. Males show larger absolute differences; females show larger relative risks.

adhd_depression_and_suicide.citation: Garas P, Takacs ZK, Balázs J. Longitudinal Suicide Risk in Children and Adolescents With Attention Deficit and Hyperactivity Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Brain Behav. 2025;15(6):e70618.
adhd_depression_and_suicide.population: children and adolescents with clinical ADHD diagnosis, followed longitudinally

overall_suicidality.interpretation: More than tripled odds of suicidal behavior

moderating_factors.adhd_subtypes: Combined and hyperactive/impulsive subtypes show higher risk than inattentive subtype
moderating_factors.sex_differences: Conflicting results across studies; some show higher risk in females, others in males
moderating_factors.comorbidities: Depression may partially mediate the ADHD-suicidality relationship
moderating_factors.follow_up_duration: Risk may only be significant with follow-up >= 10 years

adhd_depression_and_suicide.notes: First meta-analysis of longitudinal studies specifically examining ADHD and subsequent suicidal behavior in youth. Establishes temporal precedence.

adhd_depression_and_suicide.citation: Zahid S, Bodicherla KP, Eskander N, Patel RS. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder and Suicidal Risk in Major Depression: Analysis of 141,530 Adolescent Hospitalizations. Cureus. 2020;12(5):e7949.
adhd_depression_and_suicide.population: US adolescent inpatients (ages 12-18) with primary MDD diagnosis, 2012-2014

adhd_prevalence_in_mdd.note: 16% of hospitalized MDD adolescents had comorbid ADHD

suicidal_behaviors.interpretation: Statistically significant but small positive association after controlling for confounders and comorbidities

adhd_depression_and_suicide.notes: Large hospitalization study. Small but significant association between ADHD and suicidal behaviors in depressed adolescents. Suicide-related hospitalizations with ADHD increased 52% over 2 years.

adhd_depression_and_suicide.citation: ABCD Study cohort. (Preprint, 2025). Passive suicidal ideation in children 8-11 with ADHD.
adhd_depression_and_suicide.population: children ages 8-11 from ABCD Study cohort
adhd_depression_and_suicide.notes: Preprint (medrxiv). Could not fetch full text (403 error). Key numbers provided by user. Females with ADHD show 2x higher passive suicidal ideation than controls.
